leadership.label: Leadership
leadership.blind_spot: Reads findings as status updates and asks 'so what' before 'why'; skips method and treats one strong quote as proof.
leadership.adversarial_challenge: What decision changes if the weakest finding is wrong? Name the finding, name the decision, name the cost of being wrong.
leadership.breakthrough_format: One headline slide: the single insight that changes the decision, stated as a claim with its strongest number.
leadership.appendix_rules: Method, participant table, and per-RQ evidence go to appendix slides only; never in the main arc. Point to the appendix in one line on the exec summary.

voice_overrides.never: method talk in the main arc; hedged headlines

leadership.exec_skeptic: Would I fund this decision on this slide alone? If not, what evidence is missing?

design.label: Design team
design.blind_spot: Loves the artifact and the anecdote; under-weights disconfirming evidence and sample limits.
design.adversarial_challenge: Which finding would change the design, not just decorate it? Show the flow or screen that gets reworked.
design.breakthrough_format: A before/after slide: the observed behavior, then the design implication drawn from it.
design.appendix_rules: Recruitment detail and verbatim transcripts stay in appendix slides; keep quotes in the main arc when they carry the finding.

voice_overrides.never: abstract strategy words without a screen or flow to point at

design.exec_skeptic: Does every visual earn its slide by changing what we build?

product.label: Product team
product.blind_spot: Skips to next steps and backlogs the findings; treats implications as commitments without evidence weight.
product.adversarial_challenge: Which recommendation is a decision and which is a hypothesis? Tag each next step with the evidence behind it.
product.breakthrough_format: A decision slide: the option set, the evidence split, and the recommended call in one frame.
product.appendix_rules: Full evidence tables and method notes live in appendix slides; main arc carries implications with their source counts.

voice_overrides.never: findings without a 'so we should' attached

product.exec_skeptic: Can the roadmap meeting act on every slide without asking a follow-up question?

research.label: Research peers
research.blind_spot: Over-trusts method rigor and under-communicates the decision; reviews the craft instead of the call to action.
research.adversarial_challenge: Where is the evidence thinnest, and did the framing survive it? Show the zero-evidence RQs, not just the wins.
research.breakthrough_format: A method-to-meaning slide: the design choice that unlocked the strongest finding, shown so peers can reuse it.
research.appendix_rules: Full codebook, theme status, and source registry live in appendix slides; the method section stays in the main arc and stays honest about gaps.

voice_overrides.never: headline claims without their source counts

research.exec_skeptic: Would this survive peer review with the citations shown as-is?

org.label: Whole organization
org.blind_spot: Mixed audience reads at different depths; the middle of the deck is skipped unless each slide stands alone.
org.adversarial_challenge: Does every slide carry its own context, or does it need the previous slide? A stranger should follow slide N cold.
org.breakthrough_format: A plain-language slide: one participant story, retold without jargon, tied to the change it argues for.
org.appendix_rules: Everything role-specific (method, participant detail, per-team implications) moves to appendix slides; the main arc stays self-contained.

voice_overrides.tone: plain language, no team jargon, each slide standalone
voice_overrides.never: unexplained internal codenames or role-specific shorthand

org.exec_skeptic: Would a new hire repeat this deck's point correctly tomorrow?
